pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: crates/core/tests/cache_bounds.rs:6 Every test builds its fixture from scratch: `TempStore::new` calls `Storage::connect`, which runs all 56 migrations into a fresh temp DB for each test. There is no migrated template copied per test, and the build/copy cost ratio is never measured, which is the rebuild-per-test shape that fixture-economics names as the failure.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/tests/cache_bounds.rs:6 Rebuild per test (crates/core/src/testing.rs:88 → storage.rs:578 runs the migrator on every connect). Cleanup is per-test and discard-whole, which is right, but the expensive build is never amortized.

crates/core/tests/vcr.rs:3 This is a product job-replay VCR, not a test-only fixture, but it follows the technique's rules: one declared seam (AppContext::fetch); a replay miss is a typed terminal error rather than a silent live fetch (vcr.rs:14); bypassing apps are declared Unreplayable/Partial; and the tests add a second tripwire (Dead engines panic). Caveat: entries record no capture date or upstream revision. That matters little because the cassette certifies a past run, not the live service.
crates/core/tests/cache_bounds.rs:7 The tests drive the real pruners against real tables because the defect class was an unreachable pruner. A mock would have answered in the pruner's place.

crates/core/tests/cache.rs:74 The staleness check is one-sided (sleep 25ms, then require a miss at max_age 5ms). Load can only make the entry older, so a busy runner cannot turn it red. The `fill` helper's 2ms gaps for ordering are load-safe in the same way.
